metadata.title: MAPP 4160.2 Rev.1 Prioritization of Requests for Training and Visits by Foreign Regulatory Agencies and International Regulatory Organizations
metadata.legal_basis: CDER Manual of Policies and Procedures (internal FDA review procedure). Informative; not binding on applicants.
metadata.applicability: FDA staff procedure. Category: Leadership and Mission.

metadata_verification: Source-register metadata; dates and legal status require human verification.
limitations: English rule-based extraction; no GPT or paid API.
Candidates are not approved requirements. Read the original, qualifications and exceptions.
Scans, tables, other languages and implicit obligations may be missed. Zero candidates does not establish zero requirements.

candidates.statement:  If training or visits are to occur, the requestor must qualify as a foreign government official under 21 CFR 20.89 and secure the proper clearance requirements outlined by the OSO’s Visitor Access Management (VAM) Standard Operating Procedures (SOP).
candidates.context: POLICY  All training and visitor requests made by foreign regulators are coordinated by CDER’s IP staff in consultation with the FDA’s OSO, OGPS, and the host CDER Office.  The value of the training or visit, the cost of CDER expending resources on the training, the relevance of CDER’s system to the visitors country’s system are considered. Mutual benefits should be apparent for both CDER and the requesting authority.

candidates.statement:  The value of the training or visit, the cost of CDER expending resources on the training, the relevance of CDER’s system to the visitors country’s system are considered. Mutual benefits should be apparent for both CDER and the requesting authority.
candidates.context:  If training or visits are to occur, the requestor must qualify as a foreign government official under 21 CFR 20.89 and secure the proper clearance requirements outlined by the OSO’s Visitor Access Management (VAM) Standard Operating Procedures (SOP).  As part of this coordination, CDER IP staff recommend the requestor consider all- virtual meeting options before referring an in-person visit to the relevant host CDER office. If a foreign regulator still wishes to pursue an in person visit or training, the hosting CDER office director or division director makes the final determination of the request.

candidates.statement:  Foreign visitors are denied access to FDA technology systems, FDA computers, telephones, external drives, private offices, labs, and all confidential or sensitive documents. Access to FDA labs will need to be cleared with the OSO and is granted on a case-by-case basis.
candidates.context:  CDER IP staff ensure foreign regulators receive OSO’s clearance to proceed with an in-person visit. A visit cannot take place without OSO clearance.  Foreign visitors are authorized to use the guest IT network (not the FDA internal network), to provide presentations.

candidates.statement: Effective Date: 5/30/00; 11/09/22 Page 3 of 7  If an individual is staying for longer than 30 days, and if CDER wishes to provide the visitor with FDA IT access, based on Homeland Security Presidential Directive (HSPD) 12, the visitor must go through the background check process to obtain a Personal Identity Verification (PIV) card.

candidates.statement:  All official FDA meetings and trainings are in English. Foreign regulators should provide their own translators and interpreters, if needed. All translators and interpreters need to be cleared by FDA’s OSO.
candidates.context: o The desired timeframe and duration of the visit or training. o The specific subject matter experts (SMEs) and offices the requestor wants to meet with.  Security screenings and clearance requirements are met in advance of visits by any foreign regulatory agency representative.

candidates.statement:  When appropriate, brief the international visitors on the restricted access they have to FDA property, IT systems, and confidential commercial information, and inform them of the need to secure OSO clearance to access an FDA facility.
candidates.context: and within 7 days of receipt.  Protect confidential, commercial, and trade secrets, and other privileged information from unauthorized disclosure. When working with international visitors, be familiar with the procedures for identifying and safeguarding confidential commercial and trade secret information. Effective Date: 5/30/00; 11/09/22 Page 4 of 7  Enforce restrictions of international visitor access to FDA systems and some facilities.

candidates.statement:  Complete the host and escort training and registration, located on the OSO SharePoint Online home page, prior to each international visit. Unless the host CDER office has staff present, who has completed OSO’s host and escort training, CDER’s IP staff will need to escort the foreign visitors, until they leave FDA’s campus.
candidates.context:  Refer requests for training and visits for longer than one month to the OSO to ensure all appropriate security screenings and clearance requirements are met.  Ensure all requirements and deadlines, described in the OSO Visitor Access Management SOP, are met.
